system.description:
Cappadocian ancillae unable to attain sufficient mastery of Mortis to raise a zombu directly may still animate a corpse through this alternate rite, learned only from one who knows it or from written texts. The product is a thumbnail-sized, translucent “blood pearl” formed from the ritualist's own vitae, which roughly emulates the animation of a true zombu when inserted into a corpse's mouth. Practicing this rite demands at least eight levels of mastery spread across Mortis, Necromancy, and Thaumaturgy combined, with no fewer than two levels in each Discipline.

System: Creating a blood pearl takes eight uninterrupted hours and costs three Blood Traits, which must come from the ritualist herself. The player then wins a Static Mental Challenge (retest with Occult), with the difficulty set by the Storyteller according to the number of hours the ritualist wishes the eventual zombu to remain animate; the practice is imprecise; the ritualist cannot know whether it succeeded until she inserts the pearl into a corpse's mouth and the zombu either rises or does not. A zombu raised this way collapses into dust once its animate hours expire.
system.source: Clanbook: Cappadocian, Chapter Three ("Alternate Creation of Zombu")
